descriptors.definition: Base erosion and profit shifting encompasses tax planning mechanisms that exploit gaps and mismatches in domestic and international rules to minimize corporate tax liabilities. The OECD/G20 BEPS Project delivered fifteen Action Plans in 2015 to establish coherence, transparency, and coordinated solutions across jurisdictions.
inclusion: Coordination of domestic laws and international standards
exclusion: Single isolated domestic tax compliance errors
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard domestic tax avoidance through its specific focus on international corporate structures and cross-border arbitrage.

descriptors.definition: The Inclusive Framework brings together countries and jurisdictions on an equal footing to collaborate on the implementation and monitoring of the BEPS package. Established in response to globalization and developing economies' interests, it creates a broader platform for international tax standard setting.
inclusion: Participation of non-OECD and non-G20 economies
exclusion: Exclusive policy formulation limited strictly to original OECD member states
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the original narrow OECD/G20 group by incorporating developing countries as equal participants in standard setting.

descriptors.definition: The two-pillar solution provides a consensus-based framework to address the tax challenges of the digital economy and implement a global minimum tax. It updates international tax norms through Pillar One and Pillar Two to safeguard national tax bases.
exclusion: Purely domestic single-jurisdiction enterprise operations without cross-border footprints
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from traditional physical presence nexus rules by introducing reallocation of taxing rights and minimum taxation.

descriptors.definition: The international community pursued a consensus-based response to digitalisation challenges to prevent uncoordinated unilateral tax measures by individual countries. This initiative developed into the structured two-pillar framework following initial inconclusive findings regarding ring-fencing the digital economy.
inclusion: Consensus-based responses to digital tax challenges
exclusion: Fragmented, uncoordinated unilateral digital services taxes imposed independently by individual states
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from early discretionary domestic options by offering a harmonized global architecture.

descriptors.definition: Pillar One reallocates a portion of residual profits of large and highly profitable multinational enterprises to market jurisdictions regardless of physical presence. It comprises Amount A for super-profit reallocation and Amount B for simplifying baseline marketing and distribution transfer pricing.
inclusion: Multinational enterprises with global turnover above threshold and high profitability
Simplified transfer pricing for baseline distribution
exclusion: Smaller enterprises below the global turnover threshold
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Pillar Two by focusing on market-based profit reallocation rather than minimum effective tax rates.

descriptors.definition: Pillar Two ensures that large multinational enterprise groups pay a minimum level of tax through an interlocking system of Global Anti-Base Erosion rules and a treaty-based Subject to Tax Rule. It sets a fifteen percent global minimum tax rate evaluated on a jurisdictional basis.
inclusion: Multinational enterprise groups with consolidated revenues of at least EUR 750 million
exclusion: Entities falling below the consolidated revenue threshold of EUR 750 million
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from Pillar One by enforcing a floor on effective taxation across operating jurisdictions rather than reallocating residual market profits.
